correctness.rationale: For positive weights the norming-functional formula and triangle inequality give exactly the finite-simplex maximum Phi_epsilon(u)=sum_j(1+epsilon*h_j)u_j^alpha*u_(j+1)^beta, alpha=(p-1)/p, beta=1/p; nonnegative real x realizes equality over both real and complex fields. Weighted Young/AM-GM shows Phi_0<=1 with equality iff all u_j equal, including n=2 with two parallel directed edges. Compactness localizes every perturbed global maximizer in an interior neighborhood. The simplex-tangent Hessian at u*=1/n is -n*alpha*beta*L, negative definite because connected L has kernel constants. Analytic implicit function plus uniqueness of near critical point establishes a unique positive analytic maximizing mass branch for sufficiently small epsilon. Its first displacement solves n*alpha*beta*L xi=b^circ, b_j=alpha*h_j+beta*h_(j-1). Maximizing the second-order Taylor functional gives <b^circ,L+ b^circ>/(2n alpha beta). The exact operator identity (alpha I+beta S)(alpha I+beta S^-1)=I-alpha beta L yields coefficient [p^2/(p-1)*<h^circ,L+ h^circ>-||h^circ||^2]/(2n), with O(|epsilon|^3). Fourier eigenvalues 4sin^2(pi k/n)<=4 and p^2/(p-1)>=4 prove nonnegativity, and equality for nonconstant h precisely p=2, even n, pure alternating mode. Independent Green-object reconstruction from seven observed blobs, 15 independently implemented finite-difference comparisons (n=2,3,4,6,9; p=1.3,2,3.7), and separate four-cycle Green-energy computations (1/2 and 1/4) corroborated the proof. The grouped-minus-alternating coefficient equals p^2/[32(p-1)] as stated. Finite checks do not prove all quantifiers.
residual_risks: O(|epsilon|^3) is pointwise in fixed n,p,h, not uniform near p endpoints or large n.
Uniqueness concerns the positive coordinate-mass maximizer, not complex phases; positive weights near baseline are essential.
Pure alternating centered h at Hilbert p=2 has a vanishing second-order coefficient (and in fact the radius is affine for sufficiently small weights); cannot treat strict positivity as universal.

value.rationale: The spatial numerical radius is a canonical nonlinear Banach operator invariant, and finite positive weighted cyclic shifts are the natural family underlying classical numerical-radius permutation problems. The theorem computes its complete second variation on the n-dimensional positive weight space for every n>=2 and 1<p<infinity, in terms of the meaningful graph Green inverse. The formula resolves mode-by-mode perturbation sensitivity, identifies the unique Hilbert alternating flat direction, and yields an arrangement comparison from the full quadratic law. Although the two-weight four-cycle strict ordering is covered globally by a separate theorem, the arbitrary-n all-direction spectral Hessian and sharp zero-mode characterization are neither a mere table lookup nor an arbitrary unmotivated slice; they are standalone natural exact facts usable for local sensitivity/stability studies. The proof uses standard perturbation methods but the computed Green-energy coefficient and zero-mode classification are structurally informative and not established in the inspected prior Banach weighted-cycle statements.
residual_risks: The result is only local in strictly positive weights and does not yield a global permutation law.
Hilbert p=2 case and n=4 two-weight ordering are substantially pre-covered; mathematical value rests on the full p-dependent all-direction Hessian and Fourier classification.
Generic implicit-function perturbation theory underlies the method, so value is a modest but nontrivial exact structural classification rather than a broad new framework.
